children: British insurer and money manager M&G
beat half-year profit expectations on Thursday and forecast low double-digit annual profit growth, as strong client inflows from its Japanese partner Daiichi Life
cushioned the impact of market volatility due to the Iran war.
The results offer reassurance to investors concerned about client retention after the prolonged Iran war whipsawed global markets and triggered heavy withdrawals across the sector.

The company posted adjusted operating profit before tax of £435 million ($586.51 million) for the six months ended June 30, above the company-compiled consensus of £429 million, against net inflows of £2.4 billion from open business.
